chains.frame: Which word best describes Maia's business simulation?

beats.text: Maia’s game lets students privately own bakeries, set prices and keep profits after paying their costs.
beats.decisive_clue: businesses are privately owned for profit
beats.reason: Businesses are privately owned for profit is the evidence for capitalism.

beats.text: The bakeries compete for customers instead of receiving production orders from the school.
beats.reason: The added role of competition reinforces a market system rather than an enthusiasm for shopping.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: competition and prices guide production.
chains.feedback_deep: Capitalism is a system of private ownership, profit and market allocation. Maia’s simulation models business ownership and pricing; consumerism refers to attitudes toward acquiring goods.
chains.contrast_rule: Capitalism organizes ownership and markets; consumerism celebrates acquiring.

chains.frame: Which word best describes the habit Omar notices among his friends?

beats.text: Omar sees friends replace perfectly good phones mainly because a newer model has appeared.
beats.decisive_clue: people replace usable goods for newer purchases
beats.reason: People replace usable goods for newer purchases is the evidence for consumerism.

beats.text: They proudly compare how often they can afford another upgrade.
beats.decisive_clue: frequent upgrades become a source of pride
beats.reason: The pride in repeated buying strengthens the emphasis on acquisition.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: frequent upgrades become a source of pride.
chains.feedback_deep: Consumerism values continual buying, often beyond practical need. Omar’s friends focus on upgrades, not on the ownership structure of the phone companies.
chains.contrast_rule: Capitalism organizes ownership and markets; consumerism celebrates acquiring.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Laila's account of local shops?

beats.text: Laila explains that shopkeepers own their businesses, risk their own money and decide what to sell for profit.
beats.decisive_clue: private owners bear risk and seek profit
beats.reason: Private owners bear risk and seek profit is the evidence for capitalism.

beats.text: They change their prices when competing shops attract more customers.
beats.reason: Price changes reinforce market competition, but the core distinction remains private economic organisation.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: private owners bear risk and seek profit.
chains.feedback_deep: Capitalism concerns who owns production and how prices and profits work. Laila is explaining the market system, not a culture of accumulating possessions.
chains.contrast_rule: Capitalism organizes ownership and markets; consumerism celebrates acquiring.

chains.frame: Which word best describes the trend Sofia criticises online?

beats.text: Sofia’s feed encourages followers to buy a fresh outfit for every outing, even if older clothes are untouched.
beats.decisive_clue: the trend promotes repeated purchases without need
beats.reason: The trend promotes repeated purchases without need is the evidence for consumerism.

beats.text: The posts show different colours each week, but the instruction to keep buying never changes.
beats.decisive_clue: the original buy-more pressure remains decisive
beats.reason: Changing colours is cosmetic; the persistent push to acquire goods is what matters.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: the trend promotes repeated purchases without need.
chains.feedback_deep: Consumerism concerns a social emphasis on purchasing and acquiring. Sofia critiques the pressure to buy, rather than any particular arrangement of ownership and markets.
chains.contrast_rule: Capitalism organizes ownership and markets; consumerism celebrates acquiring.

chains.frame: Which word best describes the trend Mina sees in the decorating group?

beats.text: Mina watches members throw out matching cushions whenever an influencer announces a new seasonal look.
beats.decisive_clue: members repeatedly replace goods to follow trends
beats.reason: Members repeatedly replace goods to follow trends is the evidence for consumerism.

beats.text: Even people pleased with their rooms feel pressure to order another set.
beats.decisive_clue: the repeated pressure to buy remains the core feature
beats.reason: Satisfaction with the old rooms emphasizes how unnecessary the replacement can be.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: members repeatedly replace goods to follow trends.
chains.feedback_deep: Consumerism is a culture of continual acquisition. Mina observes buying motivated by trends, not the private ownership of factories or shops.
chains.contrast_rule: Capitalism organizes ownership and markets; consumerism celebrates acquiring.
